title: Oklahoma 20, Nebraska 17: Peacock's 1976 Comeback in Lincoln
question: How did Oklahoma beat Nebraska 20-17 in Lincoln in 1976?
answer: Trailing 17-7 after three quarters, Oklahoma scored 13 fourth-quarter points on November 26, 1976, and Elvis Peacock's 2-yard touchdown run with 38 seconds left sealed a 20-17 win at Nebraska.
summary: On Nov. 26, 1976, Oklahoma erased a 17-7 deficit at Nebraska behind two Elvis Peacock touchdown runs, the last with 38 seconds left, to win 20-17.
body: Thanksgiving weekend 1976 brought the Sooners to Lincoln for the regular-season finale against Nebraska. Oklahoma entered ranked eighth, Nebraska tenth, and each team stood at 7-2-1 according to SoonerStats. The temperature at kickoff was a frigid 17 degrees.

Oklahoma started fast. Elvis Peacock ran one yard for a touchdown with 16 seconds left in the first quarter, and the Sooners led 7-0. Then the Cornhuskers took over. Al Eveland kicked a 33-yard field goal, and in the third quarter Curtis Craig and Rick Berns each scored on short runs, putting Nebraska ahead 17-7 going to the fourth.

The comeback began when Peacock broke a 50-yard touchdown run with 12:28 to play, though the two-point try failed and OU still trailed 17-13. Late in the game, HuskerMax describes a third-and-19 completion that was lateraled to Peacock, who raced to the 2-yard line. Peacock scored on the next play with 38 seconds left, and Uwe von Schamann's kick made it 20-17.

The numbers show how Oklahoma won. The Sooners rushed for 357 yards on 69 carries to Nebraska's 185, and threw only two passes. It was classic Barry Switzer wishbone football. Oklahoma finished 9-2-1 after beating Wyoming 41-7 in the Fiesta Bowl, and ended the year ranked fifth in the final AP poll.
